title: The harrowing of Maga
gist: Analysis of sweeping 2026 US midterm Democratic victories — projected control of the House (at least 228 seats) and Senate (54 seats) — driven by voter anger over corruption and cost of living tied to Trump; big money, including Elon Musk's $450m+, failed to buy outcomes, and the author concludes Trump has lost his ability to govern.

insights.claim: Democrats were projected by the New York Times to control the House with at least 228 seats, above the 218 needed, and had taken the Senate with 54 seats with Alaska and Mississippi still counting.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Divided government ahead: expect legislative gridlock and intense oversight of the White House through 2028.

insights.claim: Hakeem Jeffries is likely to become the first black speaker of the House, giving Democrats important oversight of White House policy and alleged personal graft.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Congressional investigations into administration corruption become a headline risk.

insights.claim: Democrats won in places long out of reach, including Kansas, where a Democrat was last elected to the Senate in 1932, and apparently Mississippi, last won in 1982.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Electoral map realignment raises Republican vulnerability beyond swing states.
insights.locator: There were Democratic victories in parts

insights.claim: The author concludes that with this election, Trump has lost his ability to govern.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Lame-duck dynamics: executive agenda (tariffs, etc.) faces congressional constraints.
insights.quote: Because this week, he lost his ability to govern.
insights.locator: All the while, Trump spent election day

themes.theme: Drivers: corruption and cost of living

insights.claim: Voters told pollsters their choices were based mostly on corruption and the cost of living, both tied directly to President Trump.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Inflation and affordability remain the decisive political variable; watch policy responses on prices.

insights.claim: In Iowa, diesel prices are up 60 per cent year-on-year and Trump's tariffs heavily affect farmers, contributing to Democratic gains including several House seats and the Senate seat won by Josh Turek.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Farm-state pain from tariffs and fuel costs is politically potent; pressure for tariff relief.
insights.quote: diesel prices in Iowa are up by 60 per cent year-on-year
insights.locator: In South Carolina the incumbent senator

insights.claim: Turnout was robust in a country with participation among the lowest of peer democracies; in Michigan polling stations stayed open later because of long queues.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: High mobilisation signals depth of voter anger.

insights.claim: Elon Musk was the biggest spender, putting in more than $450m, around half into the Texas Senate race won by Democrat James Talarico.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Massive political spending yielded poor returns; Musk's political capital diminished.
insights.quote: The biggest spender, Elon Musk, put in more than $450m

insights.claim: Of the top 15 donors, only the Soros family and Michael Bloomberg exclusively supported Democrats, yet old-fashioned organising beat big money.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Donor money advantage was not decisive; ground organising matters more than spend.
insights.quote: Big money turned out to be a big failure

insights.claim: In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governorship by nine points against an opponent who self-funded more than $200m.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Further evidence self-funding does not guarantee electoral success.
insights.locator: Many of these wins were unprecedented.

insights.claim: Democrats reclaimed religion from the right, electing pastor Adam Hamilton in Kansas and James Talarico in Texas, who framed his victory speech with biblical stories.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Democratic appeal to religious voters could reshape coalitions in red states.

insights.claim: Democrats won in Ohio and Michigan, including Amy Acton defeating Vivek Ramaswamy for Ohio governor, an embarrassment for Trump and JD Vance.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Weakens Vance's home-state base ahead of 2028.
insights.locator: The Democrats also did well in the Midwest

insights.claim: The election produced multiple firsts, including Gina Hinojosa as the first Mexican-American governor of Texas, Deb Haaland as the first Native American woman governor, and Abdul el-Sayed as the first Muslim US senator.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Shift in state-level leadership, including in Texas on immigration enforcement.
insights.locator: Many of these wins were unprecedented.

insights.claim: The Democratic Socialists of America will be a small grouping in the new intake and may protest Jeffries' corporate backing.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Intra-party left-centre tensions could shape the Democratic legislative agenda.
